newsitem.title: USA: Union Pacific says no need to raise Pennzoil bid.
newsitem.headline: Union Pacific says no need to raise Pennzoil bid.

text.p: Union Pacific Resources Group Inc says there is no need to raise its offer for Pennzoil Co as any other company interested in purchasing Pennzoil will have to face some earnings per share dilution.
Union Pacific president George Lindahl said in a telephone interview that the company had been in talks with Pennzoil for four months and had decided finally to put the offer to shareholders.
Lindahl said that Union Pacific, which has a debt to book capital ratio of 30 percent, would finance the part cash and part stock deal with some $2.0 billion in borrowings.
"Our financial strength means we do not have any plans to sell the Jiffy Lubes or motor oils division, which in any case account for only 10 percent of Pennzoil's business," Lindahl said.

Lindahl said that Pennzoil's U.S. business had been used as a cash cow to fund its overseas development and noted that Pennzoil ranks thirty-fourth in terms of drilling in the U.S., whereas Union Pacific ranks first.
"They have seven exploration rigs in the U.S., we have 60. There are all kinds of possibilities and we will immediately ramp up their program," Lindahl said.

Lindahl said that the acquisition of Pennzoil would increase Union Pacific's Gulf of Mexico exposure. At present, two thirds of Union Pacific's production is in the Austin Chalk formation and the Rockies while 48 percent of Pennzoil's is in the Gulf of Mexico.
After the deal is completed, the main production areas for the merged company would be 20 percent Rockies, 20 percent Chalk and 20 percent Gulf of Mexico.

The deal would leave the merged company still as a major natural gas player with 62 percent of production from natural gas, against 66 percent for Union Pacific, and as a domestic U.S. player, 99 percent North America against almost 100 percent for Union Pacific.
